test_title: PYST 04: RRB Group D Official Paper GS - (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A student cuts the style of a flower before pollination. What will be the most likely outcome?

options.text: The pollen tube will grow more quickly.
The ovule will turn into a seed.

solution: The correct answer is __**Fertilisation will not occur**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **style** of a flower is a part of the pistil that connects the stigma and the ovary. It serves as the pathway for pollen tubes to grow and reach the ovary. • When the style is **cut before pollination**, the pollen grains deposited on the stigma cannot germinate to form a pollen tube. This interrupts the process of fertilization. ***Hence, fertilisation will not occur.*** • The pollen tube is essential for transporting the male gametes (sperm cells) to the ovule, where fertilization takes place. Without the style, this pathway is disrupted, and the male gametes cannot reach the ovule. • As a result, the ovule will not develop into a seed since fertilization is a prerequisite for seed formation. • Other processes like faster pollen tube growth or faster pollination are not influenced by cutting the style, making them incorrect options in this context.
